title: Biscuit French Toast Sliders
subtitle: Buttermilk biscuits dipped in custard, griddled, and glazed with syrup butter.
description: Buttermilk biscuits dipped in custard, baked golden, and sandwiched with sausage and maple glaze. Handheld, sweet-savory, and built for a tray on the table.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Biscuit French Toast Sliders in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix the custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, and a pinch of salt until smooth. Pour into a shallow dish wide enough to dip biscuit halves.

steps.title: Split and dip biscuits
steps.instruction: Split biscuits horizontally. Dip cut sides in custard 3 seconds per side—do not soak or they fall apart. Let excess drip off before hitting the griddle.

steps.title: Griddle until golden
steps.instruction: Heat a griddle over medium and melt butter until foaming. Cook dipped biscuit halves cut-side down 3–4 minutes until deep golden, flip, and cook 2–3 minutes more until centers reach 165°F.

steps.title: Glaze and assemble
steps.instruction: Brush warm maple butter on the griddle side of each half. Sandwich halves back together so glaze faces out. Hold briefly on the griddle to set the glaze.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Biscuit French Toast Sliders onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Serve warm
steps.instruction: Serve two sliders per plate with optional powdered sugar and berries. Serve immediately while biscuit edges stay crisp and centers are custard-soft.

stationWorkflow: Dip and griddle in small batches—soaked biscuits tear if stacked on a holding tray.
Keep maple butter warm in a squeeze bottle for fast glazing at the griddle.
Split biscuits evenly so sliders sandwich back together without overhang.
cleanupNotes: Wipe griddle between batches before custard caramelizes and burns.
Rinse custard dish immediately—dried egg is stubborn on shallow pans.
leftovers: Reheat sliders on a dry griddle over medium 2 minutes per side to restore crisp edges.
Cube leftovers into a bread pudding bake with extra custard and raisins.
